objective: Improve Android first-view AdMob availability and eliminate oversized invisible sponsored placeholders without increasing request spam or weakening consent, route, placement, or scope controls.
productionBaselineEvidence: Production Supabase telemetry for 2026-11-03, Android app 1.3.4/build 28/runtime 1.3.2: 477 requests, 181 loaded, 94 impressions, 188 failures across 36 sessions. First-view banner placements had materially lower fill (public_wall_entry 57 requests/11 loaded/24 no-fill; profile_first_view 56/14/42; new_home_first_view 19/3/10) than existing NativeAd placements (public_wall_feed 41/23/13 impressions; cluster_dashboard_native_sponsored 77/32/21). This establishes both AdMob no-fill and app-side presentation/placement inefficiency; it does not guarantee future inventory.
chosenApproach: On Android, replace banner-only first-view placements with the existing NativeAd-first renderer and the existing BannerAd as a sequential fallback. Preserve exact first-view placement IDs for remote kill-switches and telemetry. Move existing lower NativeAd opportunities to first view without duplicating requests. Start AdMob immediately from previously valid UMP consent while refreshing consent asynchronously; first-run consent remains fail-closed. Collapse no-fill slots and use a cooldown-bound retry.
selectionRationale: Production telemetry shows NativeAd placements load materially better than banner-only first-view placements. The client also delayed SDK readiness behind a 600 ms timer and UMP refresh, and reserved 68-392 dp empty frames after no-fill. Reuse proven native inventory, remove deterministic startup waits, and collapse failed slots without increasing request frequency.
preserveBehaviors: No fabricated ads, clicks, loads, impressions, or revenue.
AdMob UMP consent, SDK readiness, network, foreground, route safety locks, shared cooldown, remote placement kill switches, and actual provider callbacks remain authoritative.
First-view placement IDs remain stable for remote controls and telemetry.
NativeAd and BannerAd are sequential; no concurrent duplicate requests for the same first-view slot.
No-fill BannerAd remains mounted for configured AdMob automatic refresh; no aggressive manual no-fill retry loop.
Only actual NativeAd creative receives the full native media frame; banner fallback uses actual banner/rectangle dimensions.
Android-only first-view NativeAd behavior; iOS/web retain their existing banner implementation.
Connect ads remain in inbox surfaces only, never active personal/scoped chat threads, composers, calls, or search.
Organization/Cluster Wall inventory and active-scope membership rules remain unchanged.
No native package, Android versionCode, Expo runtime, AdMob app/unit IDs, Supabase schema, or production database changes.
No production OTA until CI and physical-device release gates pass.
acceptanceChecks: TypeScript, focused ad regression tests, Engineering Accountability, objective-scope gate, and Main integration QA pass.
Android first-view uses one NativeAd request with the exact existing placementId and sequential BannerAd fallback.
No first-view screen duplicates its NativeAd lower in the same list.
Only a loaded NativeAd reserves the 392px creative frame; viewport and pending native/banner probes are 8px.
Loaded BannerAd fallback reserves only its actual 50px or 300x250 creative dimensions.
No-fill and terminal errors collapse empty slots and allow only one cooldown-bound retry.
Returning users with valid previous UMP consent start SDK requests without waiting for consent refresh; first-run consent remains fail-closed.
iOS/web, Connect threads, route safety, consent, scoped placement kill switches, PG content rating, and actual impression reporting remain unchanged.
No production release claim until a verified RC and physical-device checks demonstrate behavior.
